Register a package's refusal reasons

Source: R/refusal_taxonomy.R
fb_register_refusals.Rd

A package that extends flexyBayes calls fb_register_refusals() from its own .onLoad() to add the reasons it refuses with. Its users then catch those refusals with the same flexybayes_refusal condition class as the core's, find them in fb_refusals(), and the package raises them with fb_refuse().

Usage

fb_register_refusals(refusals, package = NULL)

Arguments

refusals

A data frame with one row per reason and these character columns:

  • reason_code (required): lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Prefix codes with something particular to the package so they do not collide with others.

  • description (required): one sentence on what the refusal means, shown by fb_refusals() and used by fb_refuse() when no message is given.

  • since_version (required): the package version that introduced the reason.

  • message_template (optional, default "%s"): the message shape, for documentation.

  • registered_in_adr (optional, default NA): the design record the reason traces to.

  • plan_field (optional, default NA): the fb_plan() slot that reports the refusal before a fit, if any.

package

The package that owns the reasons. NULL (default) takes the package whose code makes the call, which is the right value inside .onLoad(). Outside a package it must be given.

Value

The registered reasons as an fb_refusals_table, invisibly.

Details

Each package's reasons go into a partition named after the package. A reason code is unique across all partitions: a code that flexyBayes or another package already registered is refused, and so is any attempt to register under the name "flexyBayes". Registering the same code again from the same package with identical fields does nothing, so a package can be loaded twice in one session. Registering it with different fields is refused. A table that fails any check registers none of its rows.

See also

fb_refuse() to raise a registered reason, fb_refusals() to list them.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In the plug-in's R/zzz.R:
.onLoad <- function(libname, pkgname) {
  flexyBayes::fb_register_refusals(
    data.frame(
      reason_code = "mypkg_threshold_negative",
      description = "The threshold must be zero or positive.",
      since_version = "0.1.0"
    )
  )
}
} # }
